role: The client main class: owns the display, resources, world, player and renderers, runs the frame loop (runGameLoop) and the 20 Hz client tick (runTick) that consumes keyboard and mouse input, ticks the client world and particles, and dispatches attack, use and dig clicks.
scope_reason: runTick's input handling and click dispatch decide every client packet a row produces; the oracle drives it through its hooks (ticksThisFrame, preTick/postTick, guiInput, gameInput) and the native client ports its order.

members.name: joinPlayerCounter
members.note: every 30 ticks World.joinEntityInSurroundings(thePlayer): getChunkFromChunkCoords over the 5x5 chunks around (ChunkProviderClient.provideChunk answers the loaded or the blank chunk, no side effect), then adds the player to loadedEntityList only when absent. It is present whenever it ticks; a dead one re-added is removed again by the next updateEntities with nothing else changed, so no row or frame reads the counter

notes: Oracle hooks in this file: startGame (Oracle.onStartGame), displayGuiScreen (JoinScreen), shutdown, runGameLoop (ticksThisFrame, preTick, postTick, wantRender, Det.beginRender/endRender, renderPartialTicks = Oracle.framePt (1.0 by default) in agent mode), setIngameFocus, runTick (guiInput, gameInput, ctrlDown for the drop key), getSystemTime (tick * 50 in agent mode), launchIntegratedServer's wait poll (Oracle.launchWait: 5 ms in agent mode, where a pool prelaunch gives way). Most fields are display, resource, profiler or launcher plumbing with no native counterpart by design (grouped as n/a). The cited survival.c functions were identified by the Java names in their comments (func_147115_a, func_147116_af, func_147121_ag, leftClickCounter, setDimensionAndSpawnPlayer); their exactness rests on the snapshot suite, not on a line-by-line reread here. lane/idxclient: runTick's chat and command keys open GuiChat (key.chat, key.command with no screen up; GuiChat's allowUserInput is false so the input block stops, and no Act op closes it: S2D, S2E, a portal or a world change replaces it): idx-chat-s1 (59 rows, 0 mismatches, play_check 0). The perspective toggle is the tape's opts (idx-tpv-s1). The riding/horse inventory branch is unreachable (horses off, world.conf).
